title: Stop the torn-read guard failing on scheduler starvation
action: a_concurrent_reader_never_sees_empty_or_truncated_state_json fails about one run in three inside the full 13-test concurrency binary and never fails alone (0.14s, green every time). The failing assertion is its own anti-vacuous guard at concurrency.rs:1012 - count >= 20 monitor reads - not the torn-read invariant, which has never fired. Cause: the monitor thread sleeps a fixed Duration::from_millis(1) per read, and under the parallel run that sleep stretches far past 1ms, so the monitor completes fewer than 20 reads inside a race window that lasts about 0.14s. Make the coverage deterministic without weakening what it proves: drop the fixed sleep for std::thread::yield_now so the monitor is scheduled as often as the machine allows, and if a burst still ends under the threshold, repeat the burst a bounded number of times before failing, so the test reports genuine starvation rather than a scheduling accident. The torn-read assertions stay exactly as they are. Four sightings today, one of them blocking a bee worktree merge.

truths: ten consecutive runs of the full concurrency binary are green
the torn-read and empty-read assertions are unchanged
the coverage guard still fails when the monitor genuinely never overlaps the writers
